question: According to the Transformer paper, what property of recurrent models prevents parallelization within training examples, and why does it matter more for long sequences?
final_text: I couldn't find this in the passages I retrieved from the three papers, so I won't guess. I searched: AIAYN §1 Introduction; AIAYN §abstract Abstract; AIAYN §6.3 English Constituency Parsing; HNET §1 Introduction.
drafts: Recurrent models factor computation along symbol positions, generating hidden states h_t from the previous hidden state h_t‑1 and the input at position t, which makes the computation inherently sequential and thus precludes parallelization within training examples [AIAYN:1:c002]. This sequential nature becomes critical at longer sequence lengths because memory constraints limit batching across examples, reducing training efficiency for long sequences [AIAYN:1:c002].

Recurrent models factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences, generating a sequence of hidden states h_t as a function of the previous hidden state h_t‑1 and the input for position t, and this inherently sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples [AIAYN:1:c002]. This becomes critical at longer sequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples [AIAYN:1:c002].
